feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Global temperature: October 2026 was the warmest October on record at 1.75 °C above pre-industrial
entry.summary: Copernicus puts the October global air temperature at 15.35 °C, 0.90 °C above the 1991–2020 average and above the 2023 record. — Sources: Copernicus Climate Change Service, surface air temperature for October 2026

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany, read 15 centimetres on 10 November, up from 11 centimetres on 9 November
entry.summary: Germany's federal gauge network measured the Rhine at Kaub at 15 centimetres at 06:15 on 10 November. — Sources: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung, Pegelonline gauge network, readings of 7 to 10 November 2026

entry.title: Queensland's heatwave warning stood at severe to extreme in the Peninsula, Gulf Country and North Tropical Coast on 9 November
entry.summary: The Bureau of Meteorology issued the warning at 14:51 on 9 November for the Peninsula, Gulf Country and North Tropical Coast and Tablelands. Mount Isa recorded 40.2 to 41.6 °C from 1 to 5 November. — Sources: Australian Bureau of Meteorology, Queensland heatwave warning IDQ21013, issued 9 November 2026 · Australian Bureau of Meteorology, daily weather observations, Mount Isa, November 2026

entry.title: Maricopa County, Arizona, confirmed 511 heat-related deaths in 2026 by the week ending 31 October
entry.summary: Maricopa County counts 293 deaths caused by heat and 218 with heat as a contributing factor, and 222 more under investigation. The counts are preliminary until the medical examiner finishes each case. — Sources: Maricopa County Public Health, heat deaths surveillance report, week ending 31 October 2026
